translations.text: A discourse on the natures of beasts, spoken from the books of Saint Basil, bishop of Caesarea.
1. There is a creature called the sun-lizard [?]. As the Physiologus said:
When it grows old and both its eyes fail, and it goes blind and cannot see the light of the sun, it [?] a certain stratagem in order to make itself beautiful:
it goes in search of a wall that faces east and enters a crack in that wall,
which looks toward the sunrise, and at the shining forth of the sun its eyes are opened and it becomes young again.
So you too, O man: if you have the old creation as your garment, take care lest the eyes of your heart go blind.
And if they do go blind, seek the place perceived by the mind, from which our new Savior Jesus Christ may shine forth upon you, he who is called by the prophet the Sun, the Dayspring.
May that Sun of righteousness open both your eyes, and in place of the old may you have a new garment.
So then, the Physiologus indeed spoke well of the formation of the nature of the species in relation to one another.
2. I will begin with the lion, for it is the crown over all beasts and all dumb animals.
When Jacob was blessing Judah, he said to him thus: "A lion's whelp, Judah, sprung up as a shoot, my son!"
And he blessed the others each in turn. The Physiologus said: The lion has three natures.

The first nature: when it is walking or strutting about and the scent of the hunters reaches it, it disturbs with its tail that track [? the text reads "bone"], lest the hunters follow and find it in its lair and seize it.
You, whom the invisible lion Jesus Christ diligently protects, he who conquered the world, shone forth from the tribe of Judah, from the root of Jesse, who came from the eternal Father.
He shone forth and invisibly concealed the spiritual track, which is the Godhead;
among angels he appeared an angel, among thrones a throne, among principalities a prince, until the time of his coming,
for he descended into the womb of Mary to save the erring race of men, "and the Word became flesh and dwelt among us."
He descended unknown to the powers above, for he descended to earth, and they said: "Who is this, the King of glory?"
Then the Spirit said through the mouth of David the prophet: "This is the King of glory."
The second nature of the lion: when it sleeps, its eyes are awake, for they look upward.
As it said in the Blessing of the Singers: "I sleep, and my spirit is awake."
If the body, that temple, slept at one time, yet the Godhead is ever awake.
At the right hand of the Father he is awake and sleepless, as "the keeper of Israel will not sleep." The third nature of the lion:
When the lioness bears cubs, she lays them down dead, and she sits and guards those cubs until the coming of the father on the third day; he breathes on their foreheads and raises those cubs up.
So too God the Almighty, the Father of all, raised from the dead on the third day the firstborn Son,
[?] of all created things, our Lord Jesus Christ. So indeed Jacob spoke well when he said: "Lion's whelp, now who shall rouse him?"
The Physiologus spoke well about the lion and the lion's whelp.
3. On valor, [and on him] who has taken up fortitude itself.
There is a beast called the autholops. That beast is fierce and savage, for it cannot be caught by hunters.
Its horns are long and shaped like a saw, for it saws through great, tall trees. And when it is thirsty, it goes to the river Pishon and drinks water.
And there are certain shrubs with slender branches, which are called tall-shrubs. And it begins to play and to butt those shrubs.
And its branches become caught in those shrubs and in their branches. They seize it and hold it fast in the branches of the shrubs.
And it begins to bellow, for it wants to escape and cannot, because they are wound around it and entangled, and it stands there.
The hunters hear the bellowing, and they come and kill it.
And you, disciplined valiant one, as long as you trust in both of your horns and saw through those branches, that is, words,
love of money and the desire of the assailant [?], the dregs of the world, the sling of the devil, the angels and powers will rejoice.
And your two horns are the two commandments. But beware, lest you too should play and butt those shrubs, and by some small occasion,
whether clothing or some other good thing, you become entangled and wound up in his snare, and the evil hunter, the devil, finds you.
4. If you are led astray by wine or by a woman, O wise man. There are stones of the plains, female and male.
As long as they are far from one another, fire never kindles. But if the male touches the female, fire blazes up and burns much country and plain.
The most courageous, those who were men of valor, Samson and Joseph, righteous men, fell into trial on account of women.
So indeed the Physiologus spoke well for the prudent, that they may be saved.
5. There is a beast in the sea whose name is Saw. Its wings are long.
When it sees ships with their sails [?] rigged, it imitates them and raises its wings like the sails of those ships, and it races against the ships for about forty stadia.
And when it grows tired, it lowers its wings and draws them in to itself because of its weariness.
And the waves lift it up and carry it back to its own former place, where it was at first.
That sea is the image of the world, and the ships of the holy prophets, who, like ships, passed through the world by means of the assault of that beast.
And its saw could not hold out against those ships. [This means] those who are courageous for a time and cannot persevere with the saints in long endurance in the good work they have undertaken,

and cannot persevere in taking up fortitude, because of love of money, or arrogance, or fornication, or adultery, or for the sake of some other good thing, which, like the waves of the sea, carry them off to hell.
6. There is a bird whose name is charadrius, which is mentioned in the Second Law of Moses.
The Physiologus said: how entirely white it is, and there is no blackness at all in it!
And the dung of its belly heals eyes that have clouded over. And the caladrius is found among diadems and in the royal palace.
If someone is sick, and that man's sickness is a deadly disease, as soon as the sick man sees it, it turns its face away from him.
By the caladrius everyone knows whether the sickness is deadly. If it is to bring recovery, the sick man fixes his gaze [?] and looks at the caladrius.
And the caladrius swallows up the sick man's pain, and the pain subsides, and the man is saved.
The caladrius as a whole is a figure resembling the beautiful Savior, for our Lord Jesus Christ is entirely white and there is no blackness in him, as he alone said:
"The ruler of this world is coming, and he will find nothing of his own in me," for he came from the holy heavens. The Jews put his divinity far from their souls.
He came to the Gentiles and diminished our sickness and pain, and he was lifted up on the cross, from where he ascended to the heights and led captivity captive.
He came to his own, and his own did not receive him. So indeed the Physiologus spoke well about the caladrius.
But you will say: the caladrius is an unclean bird, so how does it resemble Christ?
The serpent too is unclean, yet John testified and said: "As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so also must the Son of Man be lifted up."
But there is something good in the serpent, namely wisdom; and in the lion, for it is strong; and in the sheep, for it is meek.
And every created thing is twofold: even if something should be thought vile [?], yet good is also found in it.
7. David said well: "I have become like the pelican of the wilderness, and I have become like an owl in a ruin."
The Physiologus said of the pelican bird that it loves its chicks exceedingly.
When the chicks have hatched and grown a little, they crush and kill their chicks.
And afterward they mourn them out of love. On the third day they repent, saying: "Why did we destroy our chicks?"
On the third day their mother comes and tears open their sides, and their blood, which drips down onto the dead flesh of her chicks, raises them from the dead.
So too the Lord God said through the mouth of the prophet Isaiah: "I have begotten sons and raised them, and they have despised me."
The Creator begot us and we despised him. How then did we despise him? In that we worshipped created things and not the Creator.
He came and ascended the height of the cross, and they pierced his side with a spear; and he let flow blood and water, the eternal redemption.
The blood is that of which it says: "He took the cup and gave thanks." And the water is baptism, for the redemption of those who repent.
So indeed the Physiologus spoke well about the pelican bird.
8. About the owl it said: it loves the night more than the day. And our Lord Jesus Christ loved us,
who were in darkness and the shadows of death, the people of the Gentiles, more than the people of the Jews, to whom belonged the sonship and the promise [?].
Therefore the Savior also said: "Do not be afraid, little flock, for God is pleased to give you the kingdom of heaven!"
But you will say to me that the owl is an unclean bird according to the Law; how then shall we liken it to Christ?
I think it was about the Savior that Paul said: "He who knew no sin became sinful for our sake."
And "He bowed down His body so that we might be exalted." He was all things with all, so that He might save all. So the Physiologus indeed spoke well about the owl.
9. Again David said: "Your youth will be renewed like the eagle's."
The Physiologus said about the eagle: when it grows old, and its wings become heavy, and its eyes grow dim,

it seeks a spring of water and flies up, turning toward the high, fierce wind [?], toward the disk of the sun, [?] to the spring, and it heats its wings and its [?] eyes, and it comes down into the spring, bathes three times, and becomes young again.
And you too, if you have the garment of the old man and your eyes have failed, seek the spiritual spring, the commandment of the living God, who said:
"They have forsaken me, the spring of living water," and fly up to the height of the disk of the sun, the righteous one, Jesus Christ.
And He will burn away for you that old garment which you put on from the devil, as those two elders heard: "You who have grown old in evil days!"
And you were baptized three times from the enduring spring, in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
And you stripped off the old man together with his deeds, and let us put on
the new one, whom God has established; whence David said: "May your youth be renewed like the eagle's!" So the Physiologus indeed spoke well about the eagle.
10. Our Lord Jesus Christ said: "I have authority to lay down my body, and I have authority to take it up again."
The Jews were dismayed at that saying. There is a certain Indian bird; its name is the phoenix.
Every five hundred years it comes to the trees of Lebanon and fills its wings with incense.
And it comes to the city of Areg in the month of Mihrakan or of Vardoba, and it notifies the priest of the temple.
And when that priest understands, he goes into the temple and fills the temple with vine cuttings, or wood.
And that bird goes to the city of Areg, full of incense, and enters the temple, and it kindles the fire itself and burns itself up.
On the next day that priest goes in and searches over the temple, and he finds a single worm in the ashes.
And on the second day it grows wings and becomes a young bird. And it becomes as it was at first, and it parts from the priest.
It flies up and departs and arrives at its former place. But if a bird has authority to kill its own body and to live, you fools,
why are you dismayed at the word of our Lord Jesus Christ, who said: "I have authority to lay down my body, and I have authority to take it up"?
The phoenix bears the figure of our Savior Jesus Christ, for He came forth from heaven and carried both wings with a fragrant scent, with courage and the gifts of heaven.
For let us raise up our hands in hymns and send up fragrance through good deeds, courage, and orderly conduct.
So then, the Physiologus spoke well about the phoenix bird.
11. Scripture says: "Whoever speaks evil of his father or of his mother, let him be put to death" — those who despise and those who revile their fathers and mothers.
There is a certain bird whose name is the hoopoe. The Physiologus said: when the chicks see their mother or father grown old [?] and deprived of their eyesight,
those chicks pluck out their old feathers and lick their eyes and warm them with their own wings, and they renew them and make them young again, and they say to their parents:
"Just as you labored for us by laying the egg and hatching the chick, and raised us, so too do we repay you that debt."
Are people not even as much as the dumb beasts, that these, who are endowed with reason, do not take care of their own parents? The Physiologus spoke well.
12. About the wild ass Job too said: "Who has set the wild ass free?" The Physiologus said about the wild ass: it is a katabani meremake [?].
When she bears a male foal, the father bites off its genitals and makes it useless, so that their seed and kin may not multiply.
Those fathers of former times multiplied the root of their seed so that it would increase, but these later generations train their spiritual children in endurance;
they look to the heavenly life, so that it may increase, as Scripture says: "Rejoice, O barren one, who did not bear; cry out and shout, you who were not in labor;
for the barren woman has many more children than she who had a husband."
The old commandments multiplied seed, but this new one trains in endurance.
13. John spoke well to the Pharisees: "Offspring of vipers, who showed you how to flee from the wrath that is to come?"
The Physiologus spoke about the viper: when the male has intercourse with the female, he makes her conceive through the mouth.
And the female, when she has swallowed the seed, cuts off the male's genitals and removes them.
When that male thinks that he has had intercourse with the female, that male dies right then and there.
Before his death he goes back and forth to the female many times, and because he cannot restrain himself, he has intercourse with the female and dies.
But as for the female, because she has no womb in which to carry the young, when the offspring grow,
they pierce the sides of their mother and come out, and they kill their mother, and thus they are devourers of father and mother.
He rightly likened the Pharisees to vipers: just as the viper kills its father and mother, so too do the Pharisees kill their spiritual father,
their own father and mother, our Savior Jesus Christ and the Church. How then shall flight from the wrath that is to come be accomplished?
But that father of theirs and mother of theirs are alive forever, and they themselves have perished for eternity.
14. Our Lord Jesus Christ said in the Gospel: "Be wise as serpents and innocent as doves."
The Physiologus said: there are three natures of the serpent. The first nature: when it grows old and its eyes fail, and it wishes to become young again,
it stands fasting and wastes away, and that serpent fasts forty days and forty nights, until its skin wears loose and comes apart.
it seeks out a cleft and finds a narrow place in the rock, and it climbs into the narrow place and casts off its old skin and becomes young again.
Listen to the one who said: "Strive to enter by the narrow and difficult gate, which lead to eternal life."
The second nature of the snake: when it goes to a river to drink, it does not take its venom with it, but puts it down there in a den or a hole.
So it is fitting for us too, when we gather at church to listen and to drink the living, everlasting water, and to hear the divine word in the church,
and neither must we take with us the venom of this earth, full of filth and mixed with dregs: desire and thoughts of wickedness.
The third nature of the snake: when it sees a naked person, it is enamored of him, and if it sees one clothed, it leaps upon him. And let us understand this in its hidden sense.
As long as our father Adam was naked in paradise, the evil devil did not dare to come upon him there.
15. Solomon speaks a proverb: "Go to the ant and imitate it, O sluggard!" The Physiologus said: The ant has three natures.
The first nature: when they go along the road in a line, one after another, each one carries its own grain, a kernel, in its mouth, and the idle ones who have none do not say to those laden ones:
"Give to us too!", nor do they take it from them by force, nor do they envy them because they quickly gather a store.
This is the figure of the wise virgins. But woe to those foolish virgins, who were never justified.
The second nature of the ant: when it brings a grain into its dwelling, it cuts it right through the middle, lest it be winter or warm weather and the grains sprout and they die of hunger.
So you too, keep the commandments and keep your soul far from evil deeds; be on your guard.
Let the depth of knowledge not kill you, as Paul says: "The letter kills, but the spirit gives life."
Again he said: "The commandment of the Spirit has set you free," and: "The commandments are spiritual." The Jews, dead in spirit, follow the commandment alone, without the spirit.
The third nature of the ant: many times, when it goes to a grain field and climbs to the top of a stalk to crush the grain, before climbing to the top it smells whether it is of wheat or of barley.
If it is of barley, it flees from there and goes to that of wheat, for barley is food for cattle, as Job said: "Instead of my wheat let barley come up for me."
And you, flee from the Chaldeans, who have made themselves into beasts, and with every foreign teaching.
16. The prophet Isaiah said: "There sirens and demons will dance, and onocentaurs will dwell."
The Physiologus said of the sirens that they bring death upon man.
They are in the sea and sing a song with a sweet voice. And the sailors who pass by those places in a boat,
when they hear that sound of singing, listen so long and take such pleasure in it that they grow faint and are led astray, and they fall into the sea and perish.
And the form of those sirens is human as far as the bosom, and part of their form is that of birds. So too with the donkey-bulls: part is donkey, part is bull.
So too every "double-minded man is a heretic in all his ways," just as here are found [?] who do gather together in the church and yet cannot keep far from sin.
As the scripture said: "They have the image of godliness and have departed from its power."
For when they enter the church, they appear in the guise of reverence, and when the assemblies are dismissed, they take on the form of beasts.
So too the form of sirens and onocentaurs lies upon them.
They are transgressors of the law, liars and heretics, who "with sweet appearances deceive unstable souls."
As blessed Paul said: "Evil words corrupt gentle minds."
17. There is a certain moving creature that is called the hedgehog. It is round, like a ball in form and appearance.
Its back is armed with thorns, and its thorns resemble those of the sea urchin.
The Physiologus said of the hedgehog: when it climbs up a vine, it strips the berries from the clusters and [?] and scatters them down, and then comes down.
It gathers them together and rolls on the berries, and the berries stick to its thorns. It carries them to its young and leaves the stalk of the cluster bare.
Now you, O valiant one, who stand as guard and keeper [?] of the spiritual vineyard,
whose true spiritual grape has ripened and come to the point of the winepress and of being gathered into the treasuries of that radiance, to go and arrive at the holy [?] of Christ,
to arrive at eternal life: how can you allow the hedgehog to climb up to your place, to ruin it and to wither your beautiful vigor?
And with a deadly [?] the assailant of the powers will beat you and will lay waste your strength.
So the Physiologus spoke rightly and fittingly about the character of the beast that is mentioned in the divine scriptures.
18. Concerning the fox the Physiologus said: it is an utterly cunning and treacherous beast. When it is hungry and finds no prey to eat, it goes and finds a muddy pool,
or wherever there is chaff, and it rolls there, or rolls on [?] and chaff, and lies on its back. And when it [?], it holds its breath and swells up [?] completely.
And the birds, thinking that it is dead, come down to eat it.
And so by deception it seizes them, tears out the entrails of those birds, and kills them cruelly.
So too the devil is utterly small, and his schemes are great. Whoever wishes to taste of his flesh dies.
The flesh of the assailant is fornication and love of money. Herod was called a fox, and the Savior said to the scribe: "Foxes have holes."
In the blessed Song it is written: "Catch the crafty foxes, the destroyers of my vineyard."
And David said: "They will be a portion for foxes." So the Physiologus spoke well of the fox.
19. The prophet prophesies: "Lord, if I should be like a lion to the house of Judah and like a panther to the house of Ephraim, and I should be like leopards."
The Physiologus described its character in this way: that animal is beloved of all the beasts.
It hates only the serpent, and it is entirely mottled, like the many-colored garment of Joseph.
Beautifully adorned, like a queen of [?], of whom David said: "The queen stood at your right hand, adorned in fringed garments of many kinds."
The panther is a gentle, [?] and quiet beast. When it eats food, it is sated and lies down in its lair.
After three days it rises from sleep. So too our Lord rose from the dead on the third day.
And when the panther rises from sleep in its lair on the third day, it roars with a crying voice.
And in its roaring, a scent of incense comes forth from its mouth.
And the beasts that are far off or near follow its cry, from where the scent has reached them.
So too our Lord and Savior Jesus rose from the dead, and a fragrant scent reached us, those who are far off and those who are near;
he made peace in heaven and on earth, as Paul said: the wisdom of our Lord Jesus Christ is many-scented and flowering,
which is virginity, and mercy, and endurance, and faith, and courage, unity, and peace, and long-suffering, like those of the beast, the panther.
The Physiologus said that it is entirely flowered, for it has no judgment among the dumb beasts and birds. The divine books have said these things.
20. Paul the apostle said well: "We are in no way ignorant of his designs," and he said another thing as well.
The Physiologus said: There is a beast in the sea that is called vahanakra, the sea turtle.
It resembles a whale-fish, and in color it resembles the sand of a shoal. The voice of that beast is evil. And it deceives sailors who are unaware.
They go there, moor their ships as if on a shoal, set down [?] and let down [?].
And when they kindle a fire on it in order to warm themselves, that place sinks down into the depths, and the ships that were moored there are swallowed up.
And if you hang your hope on the devil, he will swallow you into the Gehenna of fire. And it has another constant trait:
When it is hungry, it opens its mouth, and a fragrant scent of incense comes out of its mouth, and that sweet scent reaches the fish, and they follow it and crowd into the mouth of that whale-fish.
And when its mouth is full, then it clamps its jaws shut and swallows those small fish.
And understand: those are the unbelievers, while the rich, very great fish are not found in the whale-fish, for they are perfect, as Paul said:
"We are in no way ignorant of his designs." And he said another thing as well: "He walks in every way that is not good." Job was a perfect fish.
Moses and Jeremiah, Ezekiel and Daniel, and all those companies of the righteous, and likewise the holy ones, fled from the great whale:
from a woman: Joseph from the wife of Pharaoh's [?]; Susanna from the two wicked elders;
Thecla was saved from Thamyris, Esther was saved from Artaxerxes, Judith was saved from Holofernes, Jonah was saved from the whale-monster.
And Sarah, the daughter of Raguel, was saved from Asmodeus; blessed Job was saved from the great assailant.
So truly the Physiologus spoke well about the fierce vahanakra.
21. Jeremiah said: "The partridge cried out to gather those that were not its own chicks, and would make them its wealth; but at midday they leave it, and in the end it becomes a fool."
The Physiologus said of the partridge that it hatches the eggs of another and calls forth the chicks.
For it steals strange eggs and takes them to its own nest, and warms them and calls forth the chicks, and it cannot sustain those chicks.
And it gathers something like a [?] and leaves them to cry out, and by that [?] it sustains life; and when those chicks grow up,
they fly off from one another, each to its own kind; they go to their own parents and leave it behind as a fool.

So too the devil carries off the races of men by blindness of heart and by deception; but when they come to the measure of the stature of understanding, from then on they recognize their own parent by knowledge: Christ and the churches.
And that devil is left behind as a fool. If today you were an adulterer and a fornicator, and tomorrow you become meek and righteous,
flee and go far away from that lawless partridge, and come to the law of God your parent and to the teaching of the holy prophets and apostles, the righteous and the valiant.
Therefore the Physiologus indeed spoke well about the partridge.
22. Our Lord Jesus Christ spoke well in the Gospel:
"Woe to those who are with child, and to those who have infants sucking at the breast in those days." David said:
"Behold, I was conceived in lawlessness, and in sin my mother bore me."
The Physiologus said of the eagle that it makes its dwelling on high, steep rocks and on the tops of mountains.
And when it mates [?], it goes to India and brings back that carbuncle, round and shaped like a walnut, precious.
And when it shakes it, that carbuncle sings, and it groans and cries out like [?], and pain does not come upon that eagle; it sits and gives birth with ease.
So too you, O man: if your soul conceives evil pain, seek for your body the spiritual carbuncle that makes birth easy,
to which no other carbuncle is equal, the unseen carbuncle that makes birth easy.
The carbuncle is Mary the God-bearer, who held the true precious carbuncle, our Savior Jesus Christ, as David said:
"The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner." Receive "that stone which was cut out without the hand of men."
If you believe that he was born of Mary as redeemer for sinners, you will have good hope; and first he covered himself with wrappings for the release of sinners.
At all times let fornication, adultery, self-will and love of silver be destroyed and depart from your invisible souls.
And when you abstain from everything, at that time you will conceive by the heavenly word, as Isaiah the prophet said:
"By your severity and your fear we conceived and bore the spirit of your salvation."
Those old commandments had an inner meaning, which reveals our hidden redeemer Jesus Christ,
for our redeemer was hidden from the false Hebrews and appeared to us, who once sat in darkness and in the shadows of death.
So then, the Physiologus indeed spoke well about the vulture. With a stone David killed Goliath;
two stones were a help to him, and Aaron to Moses, when he was slaughtering Amalek. The vulture has neither a dwelling nor a nest.
So too we, at that time, served many gods here and there, and we were in ignorance and in the great affliction of idol-worship.
But since the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ came and arrived upon us, to accept his commandment, so that we may be saved through him.
23. Eliphaz the Temanite said: "The ant-lion perished, because it found no food."
The Physiologus spoke of the ant-lion: its father's face is that of a lion, and its mother's that of an ant. The father is an eater of carrion,
and the mother an eater of hay. When the ant-lion comes forth, it is the offspring of both: part of it has the form of a lion and part that of an ant.
It cannot eat carrion because of its father's nature, nor can it eat grain because of its mother's.
And it dies, because it has no food. So too every "double-minded man is unstable in all his ways."
One must not walk in two ways, nor be double-hearted, nor yet be of two minds; it is not good if one is neither this way nor that.
So then, the Physiologus indeed spoke well about the ant-lion.
24. It is written in the Law: "Do not eat the weasel, nor anything that is like it."
The Physiologus said about the weasel that such are its form and its manner:
the female receives the male's seed through the mouth, conceives, and gives birth through the ear. If this is so, then she gives birth in an evil way.
Even now there are those who in church listen with the ear to the word of life, and eat the heavenly bread, and drink the spiritual cup, and when they go outside,
they cast that word out through the ear, as David said: "It will not hear the voice of the skilled charmer."
So then, the Physiologus indeed spoke well about the weasel and those who are like the weasel.
25. The Physiologus spoke of the unicorn: it has this nature and form. It is small and resembles a kid, and that beast is very fierce.
And one horn stands on its head. Hunters cannot catch it.
They bring a holy virgin and set her before it, and it comes and leaps into the virgin's lap.
The virgin warms that beast and brings it, made ready, to the assembly of the royal majesty.
Let just one thing be said about that unicorn: hear what the Gospel said, "For he has raised up for us a horn of salvation in the house of David his servant."
Just as the angels and the powers of heaven could not capture him, "he was all in all,"
until he came to the womb of the Virgin Mary, the Mother of God, "and the Word became flesh and dwelt among us."
26. There is an animal, the kasporios, a mouse of the dry land; that animal is lowly and very quiet.
And its testicles serve as a healing medicine. And it is found in the house of rulers.
When a hunter pursues it through the thickets, that beaver bites off its testicles and gives them to the hunter; and if another hunter pursues it, it shows him the place.
And when that hunter sees that it no longer has the testicles, he leaves it and goes away from it.
So you too, valiant and brave one, cut off and cast away from yourself every sin and desire of this world, and the hunter, the evil devil, will not touch you,
for with you are love of silver, adultery, and fornication. Cut that off and throw it to the devil, as is written by Paul:
"Render to one another what is owed: to the one to be feared, fear; to the tribute collector, tribute; to the honorable, honor."
First let us cut off hope and throw it to the devil, and only then let us follow the living God.
Peter and John, who raised up the lame man at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, had no silver or gold, for the sake of Christ, who said to them:
"Do not take gold or silver." So the Physiologus indeed spoke well about the beaver.
27. In the Law it is written: "Do not eat of the hyena, or of what is like it."
The Physiologus said of the hyena that it is male and female: sometimes it becomes male, sometimes female. It is an unclean beast, for it changes.
For the prophet Jeremiah said: "Have you perhaps made the dens of hyenas into a dwelling place for me?"
So too every "double-minded man, unstable in all his ways," is like the hyena, and even now there are many in their likeness:
at one time they enter the church, and when they go out of the church, away from the people, they have the appearance of women. So the Physiologus indeed spoke well about the hyena.
28. There is another beast in the river Nile. It resembles an otter and is the enemy of the fierce crocodile, which in form resembles a [?], and which some call the sea [?] (khvitk).
And when the crocodile [?] (khvitk) falls asleep, it keeps its mouth [?] upward. And when the beast finds it sleeping, it goes off,
comes and smears its body with mud, and when the mud dries, it enters the mouth of that crocodile beast and eats up all its intestines.
So too the invisible devil, who like Hell seized Adam and killed him,
so too our Savior Jesus Christ put on flesh of earth and descended into Hell, and took them away from him, and led out those first ones who had died.
By the proclamation of the resurrection they justified and set free. The dominion [?] of death, they shattered the devil's weapons of war.
So the Physiologus indeed spoke well: the otter is the [?dog] of the river.
29. There is a beast called by the name ichneumon, which is translated "victor."
And it is a great enemy, and if it finds a [?] fierce dragon, as the Physiologus said, it goes,
smears its head with clay, approaches it alone, and fights that dragon, and with its tail it shields its nostrils [?].
So too our Redeemer Jesus Christ took up earth, born from the ground, a native [?].
This is the very flesh of [?Christ], which he put on from the Virgin Mary, in order to kill that invisible dragon, Pharaoh, who sits upon the river of Egypt, who is the devil.
He turned to do battle with God and said to the Savior: "You are indeed God, and I cannot yield to you."
For this reason "the great one, greater than all" also became small to all, so that he might save all.
30. There is a certain plant whose name is called Peridexion, which is translated "kvishtobini [?] tree," and it is found in the land of India.
And its fruit is sweeter than all sweet things. And doves come and settle on that tree to eat its fruit.
And a great serpent is hostile to that tree, for the serpent flees even from the shadow of that tree.
As long as the doves dwell on that tree, the serpent cannot touch those doves, nor can it even approach its shadow.
And if the shadow falls on the west side, the serpent flees to the east,
and if the doves depart from that tree, or from the shadow of that tree, the serpent comes upon them, kills them and eats them.
Now that tree wholly resembles the nature of God the Father and Creator of all, and the fruit resembles his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, and the shadow of that tree resembles the Holy Spirit.
As Gabriel said to Mary: "The Holy Spirit shall come upon you, and the power of the Most High shall overshadow you."
The doves are those who receive the wisdom and teaching of the Holy Spirit, as the Gospel said:
"In the bodily likeness of a dove the Holy Spirit descended upon him." Take care, O man, to follow and to receive the intelligible Holy Spirit,
or the invisible dove of heaven, which came down from heaven in the likeness of a dove and rested upon him, so that in the same way it may rest upon you.
And if anyone does not resemble the dove in all innocence, he will become estranged from the Godhead of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.
And if that dragon, the devil, finds you empty, he will kill you.
Just as there the dragon cannot touch that tree, nor even the fruit of that tree, so also you, O man, if you have the heavenly Holy Spirit, the devil cannot touch you.
So the Physiologus indeed spoke well about that kvishtobini [?].
31. The prophet Jeremiah spoke well: "I sat like a raven, alone in the desert."
The Physiologus said of the raven that it has only one male. And if that male dies, the female does not touch another male.
The people of the Jews, who were in that land of the Jews, killed the Word of God, Jesus Christ, the Savior, their own father [?].
Henceforth Christ was not [their] father [?], as Paul said: "I have betrothed you, to present you as a holy virgin to Christ."
And they abandoned that father [?] of theirs, Christ, and "committed fornication with wood and stone."
And if you always have understanding and the word of wisdom and of the Holy Spirit, the harlot devil will not enter into you.
And if an obscene word and vain mockery burst forth from our mouth and from our minds, the assailant will enter to dwell there.
And now let us have eagerness toward the Holy Spirit and the offering of prayer, as "he does not slumber,
nor does the keeper of Israel sleep," and let thieves not enter your mental and invisible house.
Thus indeed the Physiologus spoke well of the raven.
32. In the "Blessing of Blessings" he said: "The voice of the turtledove was heard."
The Physiologus said of the turtledove that it sets itself apart and goes away alone into the wilderness and settles there.
It is accustomed to living alone and does not wish to be among many males.
So too our Savior Jesus Christ went up alone, by himself, onto Mount Tabor, "and Moses and Elijah appeared to him," and the proclamation came from above, from a cloud:
"This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him." The turtledove loves to go alone. And you, beautiful
youths, who have put on Christ, love dwelling alone, far and near.
33. In Isaiah it is written concerning Hezekiah, for he said: "Like a swallow, so I chirped, and like a dove, so I moaned."

Again he said: "The turtledove and the swallow and the young birds of the field knew their time." The Physiologus said of the swallow: at first it gives birth once, and afterward it gives birth no more.
So too our Savior, Jesus Christ: once he was conceived and born, once he was crucified, and once he rose from the dead.
"One is God, one the faith, one the baptism, one the Father of all, God." Thus indeed the Physiologus spoke well of the swallow.
34. David said with a cry: "As the deer longs for the springs of water, so my soul longs for you, O God."
The Physiologus said of the deer that it is [?] an enemy of the serpent.
And whenever it sees it, and the serpent flees and goes down into a hole, the deer goes and fills its flanks with water from a spring and goes to the hole
where the serpent lies hidden, and pours out that water and fills the hole, until the serpent comes out, and it tramples it with its feet and kills it.
So too our Savior Jesus Christ killed that great dragon, the devil, with the water of heaven, which he had from the wisdom of the Godhead, which water the dragons, the demons, could not withstand.
May God give me wisdom, that I may open my mouth and utter the praise of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever, amen.
